newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sees new talks with rebels by Saturday-source.
newsitem.headline: Peru sees new talks with rebels by Saturday-source.

text.p: Peru and Marxist rebels holding 72 VIP hostages were likely to meet on Friday or Saturday for fresh face-to-face talks aimed at ending the 58-day siege at the the Japanese ambassador's home, a government source said on Thursday.
"Today (Thursday) would be difficult. I reckon it will be Friday or Saturday," the source close to negotiations told Reuters.

The government's negotiator, Domingo Palermo, and the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) second-in-command, Rolly Rojas, met for four hours on Tuesday in a building across the street from the diplomatic mansion.
At that meeting -- the first since Dec. 28 -- the two sides agreed to carry on holding talks but set no date for future discussions.

A guarantors' comission made up of representatives of the Red Cross, the Vatican and Canadian government will oversee the next meeting at a safe house 150 feet (50 meters) from the Japanese residence. Tokyo is also set to have an observer present at the talks.

The resumption of dialogue on Tuesday signaled a breakthrough in the 58-day crisis. But with the rebels refusing to give up their demand for the release of hundreds of comrades -- a demand the government flatly rejects -- a peaceful solution is not expected any time soon.

The rebels originally took more than 500 hostages on Dec. 17 during a lavish cocktail party but have freed most of them. The remaining 72 captives in the mined and booby-trapped residence include two Peruvian ministers, the Japanese and Bolivian ambassadors, about two dozen Japanese businessmen and President Alberto Fujimori's brother.
